raw.comments:
According to https://www.nfqbyp.com/tk/yejieshangjian/15535.html, the 1953 1 fen note has 2 types (oily and non-oily). The oily type (2 Roman with Crown numbers 90 and below) were usually packaged in black oily bags, whereas the non-oily type (2 Roman with Crown numbers with 91 to 99) were packaged in plastic bags. 

 

With serial numbers: Issued since 1 March 1955. 

Without serial numbers: Issued in the 1980s to supply the demand of 1 fen aluminium coin. 3 different rare versions: 

  • I VI (18k), without serial numbers. This is because 18 is a good number in Chinese and is packaged in wax paper bag. 
  • Double stars under UV light, issued in 1993. 
  • Wavy clouds under normal light. 

Fun facts: These banknotes were supplied in gunny sacks. Each gunny sack (麻袋) contains 10 bags of 1 fen. Each bag (10k pieces) contains 10 straps of 1 fen.

 

Varieties exist in differing heights of Roman numerals.
